correctness.rationale: For any active prefix set P, the largest compatible suffix set comprises all pairs not in P whose final symbol is not a first symbol of P. Saturating with balanced completions preserves both forbidden overlaps. An independent exact enumeration over all nonempty subsets of the 16 prefix pairs, taking this maximal suffix set, gave maxima (20,36,36) for f₂, f₁+f₂+f₃ and sum f_j. Exactly twelve choices attain f₂=20, all of profile (0,8,20,8,0); their four-symbol codebooks are distinct and all their boundary pairs occur at length four. This directly addresses n=4, where only the f₂ bound constrains equality. For L=n−4, a boundary with j class symbols has 2^L binom(L,n/2−j) completions. Dividing by 2^L binom(L,L/2) yields a nonnegative weighted sum of the three bounded statistics with weights 1−r₁, r₁−r₂ and r₂, r₁=L/(L+2), r₂=L(L−2)/((L+2)(L+4)), with out-of-range binomials zero. Since 1−r₁>0, every maximizer is among the twelve enumerated sets. Every allowed boundary of these sets is completable for n≥6, so distinctness persists. This establishes the formula and census at all lengths, not by extrapolation. The central-binomial ratio tends to 1/16, and including 2^(n−4)/2^n gives density 36/256=9/64.
residual_risks: Exactly balanced class count; no theorem about longer overlaps for n>4 or other weight proportions.
